item.title: Nevada wildfire forces tens of thousands to evacuate as blaze threatens city of Reno
item.description:
Local residents look over a fence at the Hawk fire burning in Reno, Nevada, on August 23, 2026. —Trevor Bexon—Getty Images The ongoing “Hawk” fire outside the city of Reno, Nevada, has prompted the evacuation of tens of thousands of people in yet another devastating blaze contributing to one of the worst U.S. wildfire seasons in recent history. Roughly 42,000 people have been evacuated around Reno, while an additional 45,000 were warned that they may also have to flee. The evacuation is among the largest prompted by a U.S. wildfire this year, following the fires around Spokane, Washington, in early August during which roughly 60,000 people were evacuated. The Reno evacuations mark another flashpoint of a record-breaking fire season. item.title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate opinion writer fired over Charlie Kirk posts
item.description:
The Washington Post has been ordered by a private arbitrator to rehire opinion columnist Karen Attiah and hand over full back pay to the woman who issued a social media post seemingly mocking the reaction to the death of Charlie Kirk. Attiah was booted from the paper last September after unleashing a series of jaw-dropping social media posts following Kirk’s assassination. Attiah took to Bluesky to mock the public grief surrounding the killing, writing, “Refusing to tear my clothes and smear ashes on my face in performative mourning for a white man that espoused violence is … not the same as violence.” She also falsely claimed Kirk had stated, “Black women do not have the brain-processing power to be taken seriously. item.title: US public support for Iran war falls as Trump approval at record low: Poll
item.description:

It brings to mind one of George Costanza’s famous quotes in ‘ Seinfeld ’: “Every decision I’ve ever made in my entire life has been wrong. My life is the complete opposite of everything I want it to be. Every instinct I have in every aspect of life, be it something to wear, something to eat, it’s all been wrong.” Subscribe now While this might seem overly hyperbolic, it doesn’t take a genius to recognize that every decision Trump makes with respect to Iran has led to results he didn’t expect. item.title: Study: Most Mealtime Screen Time Is TV, Not Social Media
item.description:
Everyone has seen them out at restaurants: the "iPad babies" and zoned-out families. Parents letting their children, some quite young, stare at phones or tablets throughout the meal, sometimes while mom and dad also look at screens. It's easy to judge those families, though I try to remind myself that we, as casual onlookers, never know the full story. Maybe this almost never happens but tonight the parent has a crucial work deadline. Maybe it's been that rare kind of extraordinarily stressful day. Maybe that boy has developmental issues and this is the only way he can get through a restaurant meal, which the family needs to do because they're traveling. Maybe, whatever the reason, this is an anomaly and not the mealtime norm. But screen time during meals may be the norm for many families, according to some new research published in JAMA Pediatrics . Hold up, though—before you call in…

item.title: Federal Judge Strikes Down Trump’s 75-Country Visa Ban
item.description:
This January, Secretary of State Marco Rubio directed consular officers to refuse to process immigration visas for people from 75 countries because, he said, those immigrants would be more likely than others to “extract wealth” or “take welfare and public benefits” from the US. Since January, people from those 75 countries—all located in Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, or Eastern Europe—have had their visa applications frozen or denied. On August 21, though, a federal judge in New York struck down this blanket visa ban, on the grounds that it violates the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965’s prohibition on nationality-based discrimination in issuing a visa. As my colleague Julia Métraux reported earlier this year , these “public charge” bans are in part based on eugenicist ideas. item.title: Military newspaper editor says he was fired for raising concerns about Pentagon censorship
item.description:
Stars and Stripes is a newspaper that has served American troops for generations. Recently, its publisher was fired, and its editor and one of its reporters were removed, raising questions about its future. Stars and Stripes is funded in part by the Pentagon, but is protected from military censorship and control. Erik Slaven was its editor until last week and joined Geoff Bennett to discuss more.
